terms.grammar: pronoun: genitive of is (feminine as masculine)
evidence: Gell. 1.23.7: animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat
terms.comment: When “her” is not the subject of the clause: the secret animum ejus … everberat, goads her mind. When it is the subject’s own, use suus (below). ejus does not show the owner’s sex: it is “his”, “her” or “its” alike.

evidence: Cic. Att. 4.1.4: nātālī suō ipsō diē
terms.comment: As with “his”: it refers to the subject and agrees with the thing owned, nātālī suō, on her birthday.

phrases.latin: mulier fit audiendī cupidior; sēcrētum reī et silentium puerī animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat
phrases.english: The woman grows more eager to hear; the secret and the boy’s silence goad her mind to find out.

phrases.latin: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē
phrases.english: There my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthday.

phrases.latin: passer mortuus est meae puellae, passer, dēliciae meae puellae, quem plūs illa oculīs suīs amābat
phrases.english: My girl’s sparrow is dead, the sparrow, my girl’s darling, which she loved more than her own eyes.

phrases.latin: ōrō tē … mulier, sine eam tōtam integram mātrem esse fīliī suī
phrases.english: I beg you, madam, let her be wholly and entirely the mother of her own son.

sources: Lewis & Short: is · Lewis & Short: suus · Lewis & Short: ille
